title: The Little Deer Who Walked in Someone Else's Shoes

illustrations.alt: Dottie the spotted deer runs in circles around Penny the dizzy snail on a sunny meadow path, dust kicking up, colored pencil style
Dottie the deer with a white bandage on one leg sits tearfully on a rock while Penny the snail slowly approaches, other friends far away in the background, colored pencil style
Dottie the deer and Penny the snail walk slowly side by side, the deer pointing at a ladybug on a leaf with a sparkling dewdrop, golden hour sunlight, colored pencil style

summary: Dottie the deer is the fastest in the meadow — but she's never patient with Penny the snail. When Dottie sprains her leg and must walk slowly, she discovers how it feels to be left behind. With Penny by her side, she learns that the world is full of wonders when you slow down — and that real empathy means walking in someone else's shoes.
moral: Empathy means walking in someone else's shoes. When you understand how someone else feels, you can be kind in exactly the way they need.
moralZh: 同理心就是穿上别人的鞋子走一走。当你真正理解别人的感受时，你就能用他们最需要的方式去关爱他们。

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: In the sunny meadow near Whispering Woods, there lived a little deer named Dottie. She was the fastest deer in the whole meadow — so fast that the wind had to hurry to keep up with her!

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Every morning, Dottie would race across the grass, leap over logs, and tap every tree before anyone else could even say good morning. Her hooves made little puffs of dust wherever they landed.

paragraphs.speaker: Mama Deer
paragraphs.text: "Dottie, dear, today a new friend is coming to forest school. Her name is Penny, and she is a snail. Please be kind and patient with her."

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Patient? I'm ALWAYS patient, Mama! ...Well, maybe a little bit patient. But hurry up — I want to go play!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: When Dottie met Penny at the school gate, she could hardly believe her eyes. Penny moved so slowly that Dottie could have run to the far hill and back before Penny crossed the little wooden bridge.

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "H-h-hi, Dottie. I'm Penny. I'm a little slow, but I'm very happy to meet you."

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Hi, Penny! Come on, let's play tag! I'll show you how fast I am!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Dottie ran in circles around Penny — around and around and around. Her hooves kicked up little dust clouds. Around and around and around again, until Penny felt so dizzy she had to close her tiny eyes.

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "I... I can't play that fast, Dottie. I'm sorry. Maybe I'll just watch from here."

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: (muttering) "Hmph. A snail who can't even play tag? This is going to be a boring day."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: --- But that afternoon, something happened that changed everything. ---

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Dottie wanted to show everyone how high she could jump. She took a big run-up to a fallen log she had cleared a hundred times before. But today her hoof slipped on a wet leaf — CRACK! Dottie tumbled to the ground, and a sharp pain shot through her ankle.

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Owww! My leg! Mama! It hurts so much!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Mama Deer rushed over and gently examined Dottie's leg. She frowned a little, then wrapped a soft white bandage around the sore ankle.

paragraphs.speaker: Mama Deer
paragraphs.text: "Oh dear, you've sprained your ankle. You'll need to rest, and you'll have to walk very, very slowly for a while. Slow as... well, slow as a snail."

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Slow as a SNAIL? But I'm the fastest deer in the meadow!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: The next day, all of Dottie's friends raced across the meadow to the berry patch — but Dottie had to stay behind. She limped along the path one tiny step at a time, watching everyone grow smaller and smaller in the distance.

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: (whimpering) "Everyone is so far ahead. I'm so slow. Nobody wants to wait for me."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: A tear rolled down Dottie's cheek. For the very first time, she understood how Penny must feel every single day — small, and left out, and alone. Being slow wasn't fun at all.

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "Dottie! Dottie! Wait for me!" (puffing) "Please... wait... one... moment..."

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Penny? But... I was so unkind to you yesterday. Why would you come back for me?"

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "Because you're my friend, silly. And I know what it feels like when everyone rushes ahead. I know how much it hurts. So I'll walk with you — however slow you need to go."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Dottie's eyes filled with tears — but this time, they were happy tears. Penny didn't just say she understood. She really, truly did.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: So Dottie and Penny walked together. Penny was slow, and Dottie was slower. But as they walked, Dottie started to notice things she had never seen before — wonderful, tiny things that the fast deer always missed.

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Look, Penny! A little ladybug — she's wearing a polka-dot coat!"

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "I know! She naps on the same leaf every afternoon. I watch her every day, when I walk this slow."

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "And listen! A woodpecker is tapping out a song!"

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "That's Mr. Peck. He's practicing his drumming. He's not very good yet." (both giggle)

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: They found a sparkling dewdrop that looked like a tiny crystal, and a flower that smelled like honey. When you walk slowly, Dottie discovered, the world shows you its most precious secrets.

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Penny, I'm so sorry. I was so impatient with you. I didn't understand how it felt to be slow... until I was slow myself."

paragraphs.speaker: Penny
paragraphs.text: "It's okay, Dottie. You understand now. And that's what matters. That's what being a real friend is."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: By the time Dottie's leg was all better, she wasn't in such a hurry anymore. Every morning, she waited at the edge of the meadow for her best friend Penny. They walked to school together — at Penny's pace, side by side, hooves and slime trail keeping a gentle rhythm.

paragraphs.speaker: Mama Deer
paragraphs.text: "Dottie, dear, aren't you going to run ahead? You're the fastest deer in the meadow!"

paragraphs.speaker: Dottie
paragraphs.text: "Maybe I am, Mama. But the best view isn't the one you see when you rush past. It's the one you share with a friend who walks beside you."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: And from that day on, the fastest deer in the meadow was also the kindest — because she had learned to walk in someone else's shoes... er, hooves. Good night, little dreamers. Walk gently, and let your heart go slow enough to hear the world.
